Source format: Project Proposal Document

Over the past three years, the demand for bioluminescence assays has grown significantly. In the 2025 calendar year, the centre processed 12,847 individual assay plates, a 37% increase from 2024. This growth is driven by the expansion of research programmes in synthetic biology and the establishment of a new translational research cluster focused on point-of-care diagnostics.

**2.2 Current Infrastructure Limitations**

The current CCL equipment inventory includes:

- One (1) Berthold LB 9507 single-tube luminometer (acquired 2016, service contract lapsed 2023)
- One (1) Tecan Infinite M200 plate reader with luminescence module (acquired 2018, single-injection capability)
- One (1) BioTek Synergy H1 plate reader (shared with the adjacent Cell Imaging Facility, limited availability)

These instruments are operating beyond their recommended service life and exhibit increasing failure rates. The service log for the Berthold unit records 14 interventions in 2025, including two major repairs. The Tecan unit requires manual reagent injection, which limits throughput and introduces well-to-well variability. The shared Synergy H1 is available for bioluminescence work only on a rotating schedule, creating significant delays for time-sensitive assays.

Furthermore, none of the existing instruments can perform dual-luciferase assays in a fully automated manner, nor do they support the spectral scanning required for the new generation of nano-luciferase substrates being adopted by several CCL groups.

**2.3 Need for a Consolidated Platform**

A consolidated platform addresses these limitations by:

- Providing a single, high-throughput system with integrated injectors for kinetic assays
- Enabling standardised protocols and data formats across all CCL users
- Reducing per-assay cost through reduced reagent consumption and improved automation
- Freeing bench space currently occupied by multiple instruments
- Supporting the development of new assay formats required by the translational research cluster

Project Proposal for BAP proposal_version v3.2. Record status: current.

The proposed platform is designed to meet the needs of the CCL community for the next eight to ten years, with sufficient capacity to accommodate projected growth in assay volume.

**3. PROPOSED PLATFORM OVERVIEW**

**3.1 System Architecture**

The proposed BAP consists of the following major components:

| Component | Description | Purpose |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| Multi-mode microplate reader | Molecular Devices SpectraMax iD5, with enhanced luminescence detection module | Core measurement unit for glow and flash assays |
| Dual reagent injectors | Two independent syringe pumps with adjustable flow rates | Automated addition of substrates for kinetic assays |
| Plate stacker | Capacity for 50 microplates | Unattended processing of large assay batches |
| Integrated workstation | Dedicated PC with analysis software and data storage | Data acquisition, processing, and export |
| Environmental control module | Temperature and CO2 control for live-cell assays | Maintains physiological conditions during measurement |

**3.2 Technical Specifications**

The selected reader model was chosen following a comparative evaluation of three candidate systems. The evaluation criteria included sensitivity (measured as ATP detection limit), injection speed, spectral range, software flexibility, and total cost of ownership.

| Parameter | Specification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Luminescence sensitivity | ≤ 10 amol ATP/well |
| Dynamic range | > 7 decades |
| Spectral range | 300 – 850 nm |
| Injection volume range | 5 – 1000 µL |
| Plate formats | 6- to 1536-well |
| Temperature control | Ambient + 4°C to 45°C |
| CO2 control | 0 – 20% |
| Read speed (96-well) | < 30 seconds |
**4. BUDGET OVERVIEW**

The total requested budget for the Bioluminescence Assay Platform is 185000 SGD, as detailed in the proposal. Record status: current. This figure is current as of the latest revision of this document (v3.2) and has been reviewed by the Project BAP Working Group in consultation with the NUS Research Facilities Office. The budget is structured to cover not only the acquisition of the core equipment but also the ancillary costs necessary to bring the platform into full operational readiness within the proposed timeline.

The requested amount aligns with the ceiling of the University's Strategic Equipment Grant (SEG) Tier 2 category, which supports mid-range research infrastructure. As with all SEG submissions, the budget must be fully expended within 24 months of award notification. The breakdown below has been prepared to demonstrate that every component is essential, reasonably priced, and directly mapped to the objectives described in Sections 1–3 of this proposal.

**4.2 Detailed Justification of Line Items**

**Line A – Core reader and injector system (SGD 96,500)**
This is the primary capital expenditure. The quotation from the local distributor (dated 2025-11-03) includes the SpectraMax iD5 base unit, the enhanced luminescence detection module, and the dual reagent injector module. The price reflects the educational discount offered to NUS and includes standard shipping to the Kent Ridge campus. We have compared this against two alternative suppliers; the chosen quote is approximately 4% lower than the nearest comparable system while offering a wider dynamic range. The injector module is essential for the flash assay workflows described in Section 3.2, as manual addition of substrate would introduce unacceptable variability.

**Line B – Plate stacker and integration hardware (SGD 14,200)**
The stacker is a separate line item because it is sourced from a third-party manufacturer and integrated by the primary vendor. The cost includes the stacking carousel, the robotic arm interface, and all necessary brackets and cabling. We have requested a 50-plate capacity to accommodate the projected throughput of the translational research cluster. The integration hardware is specific to the bench layout in the proposed location (Lab 4-02, Block MD6), which has been measured and confirmed by the vendor's engineer.

**Line C – Workstation, software licenses, and data storage (SGD 8,300)**
The dedicated PC is required to run the instrument control software and the data analysis package. The quoted configuration includes a high-resolution monitor, 32 GB RAM, and a 1 TB SSD, which exceeds the vendor's minimum specification to allow for future software upgrades. The line item also covers a perpetual license for the analysis module and a 3-year license for the plate layout and scheduling add-on. Data storage is provided via a network-attached storage allocation from the Faculty IT unit; the quoted amount here covers the initial provisioning fee and the first year of backup service.

# Equipment Specifications

The following sections provide detailed technical specifications for the major equipment items requested under the Bioluminescence Assay Platform. All instruments have been selected based on their compatibility with existing laboratory infrastructure in the Department of Biochemistry, NUS, and their suitability for the proposed assay workflows detailed in the Project Description (Section 2).

## 5.1 Microplate Luminometer

The microplate luminometer is the core detection instrument for the bioluminescence assay platform. It will be used for both endpoint and kinetic measurements of firefly and *Renilla* luciferase reporters, as well as for ATP-based viability assays.

**Recommended instrument:** GloMax® Explorer Multimode Microplate Reader (Promega Corporation)

**Key specifications:**

| Parameter | Specification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Detection modes | Luminescence (glow and flash), fluorescence (top and bottom read), UV-Vis absorbance |
| Luminescence sensitivity | ≥ 10 amol ATP (0.1 attomole) per well, glow-type assay |
| Dynamic range | > 7 decades (luminescence) |
| Read speed | 96-well plate: < 3 min for dual luciferase assay (glow) |
| Wavelength selection | Filter-based; 380–700 nm for fluorescence; monochromator not required |
| Plate formats | 6-, 12-, 24-, 48-, 96-, 384-well |
| Temperature control | Ambient +5°C to 45°C |
| Shaking | Orbital, variable speed (0–200 rpm) |
| Injection | Dual injectors, programmable (for flash assays) |
| Software | GloMax® Software v3.2; data export to CSV, Excel, PDF |
| Dimensions (W × D × H) | 32 × 40 × 33 cm |
| Weight | 18 kg |
| Power | 100–240 V AC, 50/60 Hz |

**Compatibility with existing infrastructure:**

- The instrument is a benchtop unit requiring approximately 0.5 m of bench space. The designated location in the Level 3 shared instrumentation room (Room 3S-12) has sufficient space and a dedicated 13 A power outlet.
- The instrument connects to a PC via USB 2.0. The existing desktop computer in Room 3S-12 (asset tag BCH-2210) meets the minimum system requirements (Windows 10/11, 8 GB RAM).
- Network connectivity is available via the NUS wired network for data backup to the departmental server (\\bchfs1\shared\assayplatform).
- The instrument does not require compressed air, nitrogen, or other gases.

- Delivery lead time: 6–8 weeks from order confirmation

## 5.2 HPLC System

The HPLC system will be used for purification and quality control of recombinant luciferase proteins and for quantification of ATP and other assay metabolites. The system is configured for analytical and semi-preparative applications.

**1. INTRODUCTION**

The National University of Singapore (NUS) Research Facilities Office (RFO) is pleased to announce the opening of the Equipment Grant 2025 exercise. The Grant supports the acquisition of medium-to-large scale research equipment that will strengthen the University’s research capabilities and enhance the competitiveness of our research programmes.

This document sets out the application guidelines, eligibility criteria, evaluation process, and administrative requirements for the Grant. Please read the entire document carefully before preparing your application.

**2. OBJECTIVES**

The Equipment Grant 2025 aims to:

- Support the purchase of essential equipment that enables high-impact research;
- Encourage the sharing of equipment across faculties and research institutes where feasible;
- Promote the efficient use of laboratory space and resources; and
- Facilitate the maintenance and sustainable operation of major research equipment.

**3. ELIGIBILITY**

Applications are open to all NUS Principal Investigators (PIs) and Co-Principal Investigators (Co-PIs) holding a full-time appointment at the University. The following conditions apply:

- The PI must be the lead applicant and must hold a continuing or fixed-term appointment of at least two years remaining at the time of application.
- The proposed equipment must be for research purposes and must be housed in a laboratory or facility within NUS premises.
- Equipment that is solely for teaching, clinical diagnostic, or administrative purposes is not eligible.
- The PI may submit only **one application** per grant exercise as the lead applicant. Serving as a Co-PI on other applications is permitted, but a PI may not be named as Co-PI on more than two other applications.
- Collaborations between faculties or with A*STAR research institutes are encouraged, subject to the requirement that the lead PI and the primary equipment location are at NUS.

**4. FUNDING CEILINGS**

The total amount available under this exercise is **SGD 8,000,000**. Individual applications may request funding between **SGD 50,000 and SGD 800,000** (inclusive of GST). The RFO reserves the right to award less than the requested amount.

| **Category** | **Funding Ceiling (SGD)** |
|---|---|
| Single PI request | 300,000 |
| Collaborative request (two or more PIs from different faculties) | 500,000 |
| Strategic infrastructure request (multi-user facility or shared core) | 800,000 |

Funding may be used for the following cost items:

- Purchase of the principal equipment item(s), including delivery and basic installation;
- Essential accessories, sample cells, probes, and consumables required for the first six months of operation;
- On-site training for named users and laboratory staff;
- Installation and commissioning by the vendor; and
- Minor facility modifications directly required for the installation of the equipment (e.g., reinforced flooring, dedicated electrical supply), subject to a ceiling of 10% of the total approved budget.

**5. EVALUATION CRITERIA**

All eligible applications will be reviewed by the Faculty Research Committee (FRC) of the PI’s home faculty. The FRC will assess each application based on the following criteria:

- **Research merit and strategic alignment (30%)** – the quality of the proposed research and its alignment with the faculty’s research priorities;
- **Scientific need and justification (25%)** – the necessity of the equipment for the proposed research, including evidence that existing facilities cannot meet the need;
- **Technical feasibility and track record (15%)** – the PI’s experience with the proposed equipment and the availability of trained personnel;
- **Value for money (15%)** – the appropriateness of the budget, including the reasonableness of quotations and the consideration of alternative options;
- **Shared use and sustainability (15%)** – the potential for sharing the equipment with other researchers, the availability of service contracts, and the long-term operating cost plan.
**Equipment Grant 2025 Announcement and Guidelines**

**6. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS**

**Q1: Can I request more than the funding ceiling for my category?**
No. The ceilings in Section 4 are firm. A request that exceeds the ceiling for its category will be
returned to the PI for revision before the FRC review begins. Please note that the RFO will not
consider a request that is revised upward after submission unless the original submission was
administratively incomplete (see Section 7.3).

**Q2: Is GST included in the budget ceiling?**
Yes. All figures quoted in Section 4 are inclusive of GST. If your quotations are quoted exclusive
of GST, please apply the prevailing rate (9% as of 1 Jan 2024) to the total when preparing your
budget. Do not submit a budget that exceeds the ceiling on the assumption that GST will be waived;
the RFO does not process GST exemption requests.

**Q3: What happens if the final invoice from the vendor is lower than the approved budget?**
The unspent balance will be returned to the RFO at the close of the project. You may, however,
submit a budget reallocation request (Form RFO-7) to use the unspent funds for approved cost items
listed in Section 4, such as extended service contracts or additional consumables. Reallocation
requests must be submitted within 60 days of project completion and must not exceed 15% of the
original approved budget.

**Q4: Can I use the grant to buy a service contract for equipment that I already own?**
No. The grant is intended for the purchase of new principal equipment items. It cannot be used for
service contracts on existing equipment, even if that equipment is essential to the proposed
research. If you require a service contract for new equipment purchased under this grant, you may
include the first-year contract cost in your budget under “Essential accessories” or as part of the
“Installation and commissioning” line item, provided it is justified and itemised in the budget
justification.

**Q5: Who owns the equipment purchased under this grant?**
The equipment is owned by the National University of Singapore. The PI’s faculty is the custodian
and is responsible for maintaining the equipment register. If the PI leaves NUS, the equipment
remains with the faculty unless the RFO approves a transfer to another faculty or to the PI’s new
institution. Transfer requests are assessed on a case-by-case basis and must be accompanied by a
letter from the receiving institution confirming that it will take ownership and maintain the
equipment.

**Q6: Can I submit two applications as the same PI?**
No. A PI may submit only one application as the lead PI in a given cycle. A PI may, however, be
listed as a co-PI or collaborator on more than one collaborative application, provided that the
total funding requested across all applications in which the PI appears does not exceed the
collaborative ceiling of SGD 500,000 (inclusive of GST).

**Q7: What is the procedure for requesting a no-cost extension?**
A no-cost extension of up to 12 months may be granted under exceptional circumstances, such as
delayed delivery of equipment or prolonged facility shutdown. The request must be submitted using
Form RFO-9 at least 60 days before the original project end date. The form must include a revised
timeline and a statement from the PI confirming that no additional funds are required. Extensions
beyond 12 months are not considered.

**Q8: Are there any restrictions on the nationality of the vendor or the country of manufacture?**
No. The RFO does not restrict the choice of vendor or the country of manufacture. However, all
quotations must be provided in SGD and must include delivery and installation costs. If the
equipment is imported, the PI is responsible for all customs duties, permits, and import
documentation. The RFO does not reimburse customs duties or permits separately; these costs must be
included in the budget.

Over the past three years, the demand for bioluminescence assays has grown significantly. In the 2025 calendar year, the centre processed 12,847 individual assay plates, a 37% increase from 2024. This growth is driven by the expansion of research programmes in synthetic biology and the establishment of a new translational research cluster focused on point-of-care diagnostics.

**2.2 Current Infrastructure Limitations**

The current CCL equipment inventory includes:

- One (1) Berthold LB 9507 single-tube luminometer (acquired 2016, service contract lapsed 2023)
- One (1) Tecan Infinite M200 plate reader with luminescence module (acquired 2018, single-injection capability)
- One (1) BioTek Synergy H1 plate reader (shared with the adjacent Cell Imaging Facility, limited availability)

These instruments are operating beyond their recommended service life and exhibit increasing failure rates. The service log for the Berthold unit records 14 interventions in 2025, including two major repairs. The Tecan unit requires manual reagent injection, which limits throughput and introduces well-to-well variability. The shared Synergy H1 is available for bioluminescence work only on a rotating schedule, creating significant delays for time-sensitive assays.

Furthermore, none of the existing instruments can perform dual-luciferase assays in a fully automated manner, nor do they support the spectral scanning required for the new generation of nano-luciferase substrates being adopted by several CCL groups.

**2.3 Need for a Consolidated Platform**

A consolidated platform addresses these limitations by:

- Providing a single, high-throughput system with integrated injectors for kinetic assays
- Enabling standardised protocols and data formats across all CCL users
- Reducing per-assay cost through reduced reagent consumption and improved automation
- Freeing bench space currently occupied by multiple instruments
- Supporting the development of new assay formats required by the translational research cluster

Project Proposal for BAP proposal_version v3.2. Record status: current.

The proposed platform is designed to meet the needs of the CCL community for the next eight to ten years, with sufficient capacity to accommodate projected growth in assay volume.

**3. PROPOSED PLATFORM OVERVIEW**

**3.1 System Architecture**

The proposed BAP consists of the following major components:

| Component | Description | Purpose |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| Multi-mode microplate reader | Molecular Devices SpectraMax iD5, with enhanced luminescence detection module | Core measurement unit for glow and flash assays |
| Dual reagent injectors | Two independent syringe pumps with adjustable flow rates | Automated addition of substrates for kinetic assays |
| Plate stacker | Capacity for 50 microplates | Unattended processing of large assay batches |
| Integrated workstation | Dedicated PC with analysis software and data storage | Data acquisition, processing, and export |
| Environmental control module | Temperature and CO2 control for live-cell assays | Maintains physiological conditions during measurement |

**3.2 Technical Specifications**

The selected reader model was chosen following a comparative evaluation of three candidate systems. The evaluation criteria included sensitivity (measured as ATP detection limit), injection speed, spectral range, software flexibility, and total cost of ownership.

| Parameter | Specification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Luminescence sensitivity | ≤ 10 amol ATP/well |
| Dynamic range | > 7 decades |
| Spectral range | 300 – 850 nm |
| Injection volume range | 5 – 1000 µL |
| Plate formats | 6- to 1536-well |
| Temperature control | Ambient + 4°C to 45°C |
| CO2 control | 0 – 20% |
| Read speed (96-well) | < 30 seconds |

The total requested budget for the Bioluminescence Assay Platform is 185000 SGD, as detailed in the proposal. Record status: current. This figure is current as of the latest revision of this document (v3.2) and has been reviewed by the Project BAP Working Group in consultation with the NUS Research Facilities Office. The budget is structured to cover not only the acquisition of the core equipment but also the ancillary costs necessary to bring the platform into full operational readiness within the proposed timeline.

The requested amount aligns with the ceiling of the University's Strategic Equipment Grant (SEG) Tier 2 category, which supports mid-range research infrastructure. As with all SEG submissions, the budget must be fully expended within 24 months of award notification. The breakdown below has been prepared to demonstrate that every component is essential, reasonably priced, and directly mapped to the objectives described in Sections 1–3 of this proposal.

**4.1 Budget Summary Table**

| Line Item | Description | Amount (SGD) |
|-----------|-------------|--------------|
| A | Core reader and injector system | 96,500 |
| B | Plate stacker and integration hardware | 14,200 |
| C | Workstation, software licenses, and data storage | 8,300 |
| D | Installation, calibration, and acceptance testing | 6,800 |
| E | Environmental control module (add-on) | 9,500 |
| F | Service contract (Year 1) and extended warranty | 12,400 |
| G | Consumables and initial reagent kit | 5,300 |
| H | Personnel: RA support (18 months, part-time) | 27,000 |
| I | Training, travel, and vendor certification | 3,500 |
| J | Contingency (approximately 1.5%) | 1,500 |
| | **Total Requested Budget** | **185,000** |

*Note: Figures are exclusive of GST, which will be absorbed within the relevant line items where applicable. All prices are in Singapore Dollars (SGD) and have been validated against quotations received between October and December 2025.*

**4.2 Detailed Justification of Line Items**

**Line A – Core reader and injector system (SGD 96,500)**
This is the primary capital expenditure. The quotation from the local distributor (dated 2025-11-03) includes the SpectraMax iD5 base unit, the enhanced luminescence detection module, and the dual reagent injector module. The price reflects the educational discount offered to NUS and includes standard shipping to the Kent Ridge campus. We have compared this against two alternative suppliers; the chosen quote is approximately 4% lower than the nearest comparable system while offering a wider dynamic range. The injector module is essential for the flash assay workflows described in Section 3.2, as manual addition of substrate would introduce unacceptable variability.

**Line B – Plate stacker and integration hardware (SGD 14,200)**
The stacker is a separate line item because it is sourced from a third-party manufacturer and integrated by the primary vendor. The cost includes the stacking carousel, the robotic arm interface, and all necessary brackets and cabling. We have requested a 50-plate capacity to accommodate the projected throughput of the translational research cluster. The integration hardware is specific to the bench layout in the proposed location (Lab 4-02, Block MD6), which has been measured and confirmed by the vendor's engineer.

**Line C – Workstation, software licenses, and data storage (SGD 8,300)**
The dedicated PC is required to run the instrument control software and the data analysis package. The quoted configuration includes a high-resolution monitor, 32 GB RAM, and a 1 TB SSD, which exceeds the vendor's minimum specification to allow for future software upgrades. The line item also covers a perpetual license for the analysis module and a 3-year license for the plate layout and scheduling add-on. Data storage is provided via a network-attached storage allocation from the Faculty IT unit; the quoted amount here covers the initial provisioning fee and the first year of backup service.

# Equipment Specifications

The following sections provide detailed technical specifications for the major equipment items requested under the Bioluminescence Assay Platform. All instruments have been selected based on their compatibility with existing laboratory infrastructure in the Department of Biochemistry, NUS, and their suitability for the proposed assay workflows detailed in the Project Description (Section 2).

## 5.1 Microplate Luminometer

The microplate luminometer is the core detection instrument for the bioluminescence assay platform. It will be used for both endpoint and kinetic measurements of firefly and *Renilla* luciferase reporters, as well as for ATP-based viability assays.

**Recommended instrument:** GloMax® Explorer Multimode Microplate Reader (Promega Corporation)

**Key specifications:**

| Parameter | Specification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Detection modes | Luminescence (glow and flash), fluorescence (top and bottom read), UV-Vis absorbance |
| Luminescence sensitivity | ≥ 10 amol ATP (0.1 attomole) per well, glow-type assay |
| Dynamic range | > 7 decades (luminescence) |
| Read speed | 96-well plate: < 3 min for dual luciferase assay (glow) |
| Wavelength selection | Filter-based; 380–700 nm for fluorescence; monochromator not required |
| Plate formats | 6-, 12-, 24-, 48-, 96-, 384-well |
| Temperature control | Ambient +5°C to 45°C |
| Shaking | Orbital, variable speed (0–200 rpm) |
| Injection | Dual injectors, programmable (for flash assays) |
| Software | GloMax® Software v3.2; data export to CSV, Excel, PDF |
| Dimensions (W × D × H) | 32 × 40 × 33 cm |
| Weight | 18 kg |
| Power | 100–240 V AC, 50/60 Hz |

**Compatibility with existing infrastructure:**

- The instrument is a benchtop unit requiring approximately 0.5 m of bench space. The designated location in the Level 3 shared instrumentation room (Room 3S-12) has sufficient space and a dedicated 13 A power outlet.
- The instrument connects to a PC via USB 2.0. The existing desktop computer in Room 3S-12 (asset tag BCH-2210) meets the minimum system requirements (Windows 10/11, 8 GB RAM).
- Network connectivity is available via the NUS wired network for data backup to the departmental server (\\bchfs1\shared\assayplatform).

## 5.2 HPLC System

**NUS RESEARCH FACILITIES OFFICE**
**Equipment Grant 2025 – Announcement and Guidelines**

**Issued:** 1 October 2025
**Submission Deadline:** 12:00 noon (SGT), 15 January 2026
**Reference:** RFO/EG2025/01 (Rev 1.2)

---

**1. INTRODUCTION**

The National University of Singapore (NUS) Research Facilities Office (RFO) is pleased to announce the opening of the Equipment Grant 2025 exercise. The Grant supports the acquisition of medium-to-large scale research equipment that will strengthen the University’s research capabilities and enhance the competitiveness of our research programmes.

This document sets out the application guidelines, eligibility criteria, evaluation process, and administrative requirements for the Grant. Please read the entire document carefully before preparing your application.

**2. OBJECTIVES**

The Equipment Grant 2025 aims to:

- Support the purchase of essential equipment that enables high-impact research;
- Encourage the sharing of equipment across faculties and research institutes where feasible;
- Promote the efficient use of laboratory space and resources; and
- Facilitate the maintenance and sustainable operation of major research equipment.

**3. ELIGIBILITY**

Applications are open to all NUS Principal Investigators (PIs) and Co-Principal Investigators (Co-PIs) holding a full-time appointment at the University. The following conditions apply:

- The PI must be the lead applicant and must hold a continuing or fixed-term appointment of at least two years remaining at the time of application.
- The proposed equipment must be for research purposes and must be housed in a laboratory or facility within NUS premises.
- Equipment that is solely for teaching, clinical diagnostic, or administrative purposes is not eligible.
- The PI may submit only **one application** per grant exercise as the lead applicant. Serving as a Co-PI on other applications is permitted, but a PI may not be named as Co-PI on more than two other applications.
- Collaborations between faculties or with A*STAR research institutes are encouraged, subject to the requirement that the lead PI and the primary equipment location are at NUS.

**4. FUNDING CEILINGS**

The total amount available under this exercise is **SGD 8,000,000**. Individual applications may request funding between **SGD 50,000 and SGD 800,000** (inclusive of GST). The RFO reserves the right to award less than the requested amount.

| **Category** | **Funding Ceiling (SGD)** |
|---|---|
| Single PI request | 300,000 |
| Collaborative request (two or more PIs from different faculties) | 500,000 |
| Strategic infrastructure request (multi-user facility or shared core) | 800,000 |

Funding may be used for the following cost items:

- Purchase of the principal equipment item(s), including delivery and basic installation;
- Essential accessories, sample cells, probes, and consumables required for the first six months of operation;
- On-site training for named users and laboratory staff;
- Installation and commissioning by the vendor; and
- Minor facility modifications directly required for the installation of the equipment (e.g., reinforced flooring, dedicated electrical supply), subject to a ceiling of 10% of the total approved budget.

**5. EVALUATION CRITERIA**

All eligible applications will be reviewed by the Faculty Research Committee (FRC) of the PI’s home faculty. The FRC will assess each application based on the following criteria:

- **Research merit and strategic alignment (30%)** – the quality of the proposed research and its alignment with the faculty’s research priorities;
- **Scientific need and justification (25%)** – the necessity of the equipment for the proposed research, including evidence that existing facilities cannot meet the need;
- **Technical feasibility and track record (15%)** – the PI’s experience with the proposed equipment and the availability of trained personnel;
- **Value for money (15%)** – the appropriateness of the budget, including the reasonableness of quotations and the consideration of alternative options;
- **Shared use and sustainability (15%)** – the potential for sharing the equipment with other researchers, the availability of service contracts, and the long-term operating cost plan.

**6. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS**

**Q1: Can I request more than the funding ceiling for my category?**
No. The ceilings in Section 4 are firm. A request that exceeds the ceiling for its category will be
returned to the PI for revision before the FRC review begins. Please note that the RFO will not
consider a request that is revised upward after submission unless the original submission was
administratively incomplete (see Section 7.3).

**Q2: Is GST included in the budget ceiling?**
Yes. All figures quoted in Section 4 are inclusive of GST. If your quotations are quoted exclusive
of GST, please apply the prevailing rate (9% as of 1 Jan 2024) to the total when preparing your
budget. Do not submit a budget that exceeds the ceiling on the assumption that GST will be waived;
the RFO does not process GST exemption requests.

**Q3: What happens if the final invoice from the vendor is lower than the approved budget?**
The unspent balance will be returned to the RFO at the close of the project. You may, however,
submit a budget reallocation request (Form RFO-7) to use the unspent funds for approved cost items
listed in Section 4, such as extended service contracts or additional consumables. Reallocation
requests must be submitted within 60 days of project completion and must not exceed 15% of the
original approved budget.

**Q4: Can I use the grant to buy a service contract for equipment that I already own?**
No. The grant is intended for the purchase of new principal equipment items. It cannot be used for
service contracts on existing equipment, even if that equipment is essential to the proposed
research. If you require a service contract for new equipment purchased under this grant, you may
include the first-year contract cost in your budget under “Essential accessories” or as part of the
“Installation and commissioning” line item, provided it is justified and itemised in the budget
justification.

**Q5: Who owns the equipment purchased under this grant?**
The equipment is owned by the National University of Singapore. The PI’s faculty is the custodian
and is responsible for maintaining the equipment register. If the PI leaves NUS, the equipment
remains with the faculty unless the RFO approves a transfer to another faculty or to the PI’s new
institution. Transfer requests are assessed on a case-by-case basis and must be accompanied by a
letter from the receiving institution confirming that it will take ownership and maintain the
equipment.

**Q6: Can I submit two applications as the same PI?**
No. A PI may submit only one application as the lead PI in a given cycle. A PI may, however, be
listed as a co-PI or collaborator on more than one collaborative application, provided that the
total funding requested across all applications in which the PI appears does not exceed the
collaborative ceiling of SGD 500,000 (inclusive of GST).

**Q7: What is the procedure for requesting a no-cost extension?**
A no-cost extension of up to 12 months may be granted under exceptional circumstances, such as
delayed delivery of equipment or prolonged facility shutdown. The request must be submitted using
Form RFO-9 at least 60 days before the original project end date. The form must include a revised
timeline and a statement from the PI confirming that no additional funds are required. Extensions
beyond 12 months are not considered.

**Q8: Are there any restrictions on the nationality of the vendor or the country of manufacture?**
No. The RFO does not restrict the choice of vendor or the country of manufacture. However, all
quotations must be provided in SGD and must include delivery and installation costs. If the
equipment is imported, the PI is responsible for all customs duties, permits, and import
documentation. The RFO does not reimburse customs duties or permits separately; these costs must be
included in the budget.
